met_analysis:
The Cyclonic Storm “Murasu” [Pronunciation: Murasu]” over south coastal Andhra Pradesh moved north- northwestwards with a speed of 07 kmph during past 06 hours and lies centered at 1730 hours IST of today the 03rd November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 16.2°N and Longitude 80.0°E about 70 km west- southwest of Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh), 70 km south-southwest of Nandigama (Andhra Pradesh), 120 km southeast of Nalgonda (Telangana), 120 km south of Khammam (Telangana) and 190 km south-southwest of Bhadrachalam (Telangana). The maximum sustained wind speed was 65-75 gusting to 85 kmph at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 3rd November 2026. The Cyclonic Storm is very likely to continue to move north- northwestwards and weaken into a deep depression (wind speed reaching 55-65 kmph gusting to 75 kmph) by midnight of today, the 3rd November, 2026.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over North Haryana & neighbourhood persists and now lies at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Lakshadweep & neighbourhood extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Coastal Karnataka & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over South Tamil Nadu & neighbourhood upto 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
